cards: Hattusili III was a king of the Hittite Empire in the thirteenth century BCE.
r. c. 1267–1237 BCE · Ancient Near East
Ramesses II was a pharaoh of the Nineteenth Dynasty of the Egyptian New Kingdom, who reigned for much of the thirteenth century BCE.
Merneptah was the fourth king of the 19th Dynasty of Egypt, son and successor of Ramesses II.
r. c. 1213–1203 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Tudhaliya IV was a king of the Hittite Empire in the thirteenth century BCE, one of its last significant rulers.
r. c. 1237–1209 BCE · Ancient Near East
Tukulti-Ninurta I was a king of Assyria in the thirteenth century BCE, one of the most powerful rulers of the Middle Assyrian period.
Fu Hao was a consort of the Shang king Wu Ding who also led armies in the field, as oracle-bone inscriptions record.
d. c. 1200 BCE · Central & East Asia
Suppiluliuma II was the last known king of the Hittite Empire, reigning from about 1207 BCE.
r. from c. 1207 BCE · Ancient Near East
Wu Ding was a king of the Shang dynasty who reigned for several decades in the thirteenth century BCE from the capital at Yinxu, near Anyang.
Nefertari, also Nefertari Meritmut, was an Egyptian queen and the first of the Great Royal Wives of Ramesses the Great, whom she married before he became king.
Alaksandu was a king of Wilusa in north-western Anatolia in the early 13th century BCE, known from a treaty he made with the Hittite king Muwatalli II around 1280 BCE.
r. c. 1280 BCE · Ancient Near East
Puduhepa was a Hittite queen of the 13th century BCE, wife of Hattusili III and the daughter of a priest of Lawazantiya in Kizzuwatna.
fl. 13th century BCE · Ancient Near East
Tarkasnawa was a king of Mira, a western Anatolian vassal kingdom of the Hittites, in the late 13th century BCE.
late 13th century BCE · Ancient Near East
